verdicts.note: S4: 'ensure that the rich pay their fair share, while cutting taxes for regular people'. He does not name ESSB 6346. +1/medium.

'We need more community policing' plus claimed crime reductions in hot spots (pole_a), with treatment funding (pole_b). -1/medium is a fair net. The score's citations rest on S4 statements, not on his police-union endorsements.
Councilmember since 2021 and Deputy Mayor; not a long legislative tenure, so -1.
Co-sponsored Tacoma Ordinance 29105 (S6) and wrote 'We need to fight back' (S1). Record plus statement.
'I'll champion Universal Healthcare for all' (S1), repeated on S2 and S4. Repeated explicit statements support +2/high.

Explicit pledge on reproductive rights only. +1/medium is defensible, though Perez (Position 1) and Anderson (Senate) get +2/medium for comparable single-topic or two-topic statements. The coordinator may want to align these.

S4 is entirely pole_b: root causes, early intervention and treatment, co-response, youth restorative justice, prisons that 'change behavior', and public-defense funding, with no enforcement or staffing plank. +2 at medium (platform only) holds.
'Combat any rollbacks ... support a just transition to a clean energy future'. General, so +1.
No elected office beyond PCO, but a long state-agency policy career, so +1 rather than +2.
General support for protections for immigrants and refugees, so +1.
'Work toward real universal healthcare' alongside strengthening Apple Health, so +1 (Bushnell's unqualified pledge is +2).
Data privacy for Apple Health users is in pole_b's 'data privacy'. One explicit plank, narrow in scope, so +1/medium.
